newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells Hong Kong democracy activists to leave.
newsitem.headline: China tells Hong Kong democracy activists to leave.

text.p: China has ordered two Hong Kong democracy activists to leave the country after they tried to petition Beijing officials, Hong Kong sources and Chinese media said on Friday.

Beijing police had warned Wong Chung-ki and Chui Pak-tai, both members of local councils in the British colony, to leave China, the official Xinhua news agency said. It was not known if they had left.

Hong Kong sources said the two were political activists who had hoped to present a petition to officials, on what they said were "undemocratic" methods used to select the first post-colonial chief executive of Hong Kong.
Beijing resumes control of the British colony on July 1, 1997.
"The Beijing Public Security Department issued a warning to Chui and Wong, asking them to return (to) Hong Kong within a stated time," Xinhua said.
Hotel officials had filed a public disturbance complaint against the two for distributing materials in the main hall of the Beijing Asia Hotel on Thursday evening, the agency said.
They had planned to present the petition, along with another on the fate of Hong Kong's elected legislature, to China's top Hong Kong official Lu Ping, the Hong Kong sources said.

Copies of the petitions obtained by Reuters accused the Chinese authorities of using undemocratic methods to choose the chief executive, who is to be appointed by a committee currently being selected in Beijing.
Chinese authorities had barred two other Hong Kong pro-democracy advocates from entering the country on Thursday, one of the activists said in Hong Kong.
Officials at the Sha Tau Kok border post refused entry to Andrew To and Chan Kwok-leung of the Democratic Party after keeping them in a room for two hours, To told Reuters.
